lag_note: 1.4.7 is the live binary and the clone's pin, so no lag is acknowledged. Everything that could be re-captured was, first-hand: the changelog feed (the 1.4.6 section arrived), the --help surface (30 commands, byte-identical), the 60-name advertised list (byte-identical), the twelve model declarations (byte-identical with --sandbox), the seven custom-agent declarations (CHANGED: toolSummary/toolAction dropped, descriptions reworded, minLength/enum/maxItems constraints added) and the remote-control descriptor (79 RPCs - ListAgents and GetChangelistStatus were appended). Still unverified against 1.4.7: the tool result texts (they need a tool-using turn under a pty harness) and the seeds/Ghidra project (the reverse-engineering pipeline is a separate cycle, and every address moves on every release).

artifacts.how: agy changelog > internal/cli/testdata/changelog_reference.txt, then update the five constants in internal/cli/changelog_data_test.go (byte length, line count, section count, bullet count, sha256) and regenerate this lock. At 1.4.7 the feed's newest section is 1.4.6 - the 1.4.7 release notes are not in the feed yet; the capture grew by that section (11 bullets, 174,284 bytes / 1,007 lines / 77 sections / 854 bullets) and every other byte is unchanged

the full system prompt of a live agy request body, recorded through the clone's own proxy (internal/agyproxy, OPENAGY_CAPTURE_DIR). It is the reference for every static section. Re-verified at 1.4.7: the eight static sections (identity, terminal_sandbox, artifacts, conversation_transcript, guidelines, communication_style, slash_commands, messaging) are byte-identical to a live 1.4.7 request body - the <terminal_sandbox> section and the run_command BypassSandbox parameter are conditional on --sandbox, not on the version, and with --sandbox the whole surface matches. The environment-driven sections (skills, subagents, user_rules, user_information) differ because the machine's skill set and this repository's AGENTS.md changed, not because the reference changed. To refresh: re-record a request body against the new binary, then rebuild internal/agyprompt/sections/*.txt from it

re-recorded alongside capture_1.4.6.txt in the same proxy run; it carries the os_version / workspaces / subagents / skills / user_rules inputs Build() is fed. Not re-recorded at 1.4.7 - the skill list has to be re-discovered from the filesystem, not parsed back out of the rendered prompt, so the pair stays at the 1.4.6 inputs it was recorded with

the <user_rules> block of a controlled probe request body. The block's own bytes are from 1.4.5; the rendering it pins was re-verified at 1.4.6 by the byte-identity of the whole 70,853-byte prompt (capture_1.4.6.txt) - preamble wording, user_global labels, plugin rules and the 24 KB truncation marker included. At 1.4.7 the <RULE[path]> wrapper renders the same way, but this machine's rules no longer reach the 24 KB truncation threshold, so that path was not re-exercised

capture a streamGenerateContent body (the clone's own proxy or a CLOUD_CODE_URL mock) and extract request.tools[*].functionDeclarations; it must stay twelve, in the captured order, with the same required fields. run the real agy in a workspace with .agents/agents/<name>.md and --agent <name>, through the clone's own proxy, and extract request.tools[*].functionDeclarations. It must stay seven, in order. CHANGED at 1.4.7: toolSummary/toolAction are gone from all seven declarations, the descriptions were reworded to the current wording, and the schemas gained minLength, the AspectRatio/Action enums and maxItems. The old wording is still in the 1.4.7 binary - it belongs to the reference's subagent surface, not to this one

extract the uncompressed FileDescriptorProto for google/gca/aicode/v1main/remote_agent_proxy.proto from the agy binary (see out/local-macos/protos/README.md) and emit one <RPC>\t<Request>\t<Response> line per method; TestReferenceRPCMethodsMatchFixture pins the order. Seventy-nine methods at 1.4.7 (1.4.7 appended ListAgents and GetChangelistStatus); the 1.4.6, 1.4.5 and 1.4.4 captures remain on disk as the previous releases' evidence

decode the FileDescriptorProto at the offset named in out/local-macos/protos/README.md with descriptor_pb2 and print it with text_format; the offset moves on every agy release, and the naive top-level field walk overshoots the public descriptor - the syntax:"proto3" marker is the reliable end

cd rea-go-seeds && mkdir -p <outdir> && go run . ~/.local/bin/agy <outdir>. Every address moves on every agy release, so the Ghidra project (out/local-macos/proj) and the decompiled output (out/local-macos/dec/) have to be rebuilt from this file; the committed decompile reports carry the addresses this file held when they were written.
